title.zh: 卷一百十七 列傳第五十五: 徒單益都 粘哥荊山附:劉均 王賓附:王進等 國用安 時青
title.en: Volume 117 Biographies 55: Tudan Yidou, Zhan Gejingshan relative: Liujun, Wang Bin relative: Wang Jindeng, Guo Yongan, Shi Qing
title.raw: 卷一百十七 列傳第五十五: 徒單益都 粘哥荊山附:劉均 王賓附:王進等 國用安 時青 Volume 117 Biographies 55: Tudan Yidou, Zhan Gejingshan relative: Liujun, Wang Bin relative: Wang Jindeng, Guo Yongan, Shi Qing

sentences.zh: 徒單益都

translations.literal: Tudan Yidu
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yidu

sentences.zh: 徒單益都，不詳其履歷，嘗累官為延安總管。

translations.literal: Tudan Yidu — his career is not recorded in detail; he had repeatedly held office and once served as commander-in-chief of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yidu's background is unclear, but he had risen through repeated appointments and had served as Yan'an commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正大九年正月，行省事於徐州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Zhengda, he exercised provincial authority at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengda 9 (1232), he took up provincial duties at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時慶山奴撤東方之備入援，未至睢州，徐、邳義勝軍總領侯進、杜政、張興率本軍降大兵於永州。

translations.literal: At that time Qing Shannu had withdrawn the eastern defenses to bring relief; before he reached Suizhou, Hou Jin, Du Zheng, and Zhang Xing, commanders of the Yisheng Army of Xu and Pi, led their forces to surrender to the great army at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Qing Shannu was pulling eastern garrisons westward to reinforce the capital, his column had not yet reached Suizhou when Hou Jin, Du Zheng, and Zhang Xing of the Xu–Pi Yisheng Army surrendered their units to the Mongols at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，大兵守徐張盆渡。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the great army held Zhangpen Ford in Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, Mongol forces occupied Zhangpen Ford near Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 益都到官才三日，懼兵少不能守，即令移剌長壽率甲士千人迎大兵。

translations.literal: Yidu had been in office only three days; fearing his troops were too few to hold the city, he immediately ordered Yelü Changshou to lead a thousand armored soldiers to welcome the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Only three days after taking office, Yidu, fearing he lacked the strength to defend the city, sent Yelü Changshou with a thousand armored men to go out and receive the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 長壽軍無紀律，大兵掩之，一軍皆覆，徐危甚。

translations.literal: Changshou's troops had no discipline; the great army fell upon them, and the whole force was destroyed; Xu was in grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: Changshou's men were undisciplined; the Mongols struck them by surprise and wiped out the entire detachment, leaving Xuzhou in dire straits.

sentences.zh: 益都籍州人及運糧埽兵得萬人。

translations.literal: Yidu enrolled men of the prefecture and grain-transport labor troops, obtaining ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu drafted local men and grain-barge labor troops until he had ten thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大兵傅城，燒南關而去。

translations.literal: On yisi, the great army pressed the city, burned the southern gate quarter, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Mongols pressed the siege, torched the southern suburb, and then drew off.

sentences.zh: 侯進既降北，即以為京東行省，進遂請千人來襲。

translations.literal: Hou Jin having already surrendered to the north, he was made Eastern Hebei provincial commissioner; Jin then requested a thousand men to come and raid.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jin defected to the Mongols, they made him Eastern Hebei commissioner, and he then asked for a thousand men to raid Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申，未明，大兵坎南城而上，守者皆散走，城中大呼曰：「大兵入南門矣！

translations.literal: On gengshen in the second month, before dawn, the great army tunneled up through the southern wall; the defenders all scattered and fled, and in the city they shouted, "The great army has entered the southern gate!"
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the second month, before daybreak, Mongol troops broke in through the southern wall; the garrison broke and ran as the city cried out that the enemy had entered the south gate.

sentences.zh: 」益都聞之不及甲，率州署夜直兵三百，由黃樓而南，力戰禦敵。

translations.literal: " Hearing this, Yidu had no time to arm himself; he led three hundred night-duty soldiers of the prefectural office south through Huanglou Tower and fought the enemy with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu, hearing the alarm, had no time to don armor; he led three hundred night guards from the yamen south through Huanglou and fought the enemy head-on.

sentences.zh: 亂定，遷賞有差。

translations.literal: When the turmoil subsided, promotions and rewards were distributed according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored, men were promoted and rewarded according to their deeds.

sentences.zh: 由是軍勢稍振，複奪張盆渡，取蕭縣，破白塔，戰于土山，救被俘老幼五千還徐。

translations.literal: Thereafter the army's morale revived somewhat; they retook Zhangpen Ford, seized Xiao County, broke White Tower, fought at Tushan, and rescued five thousand captured old and young back to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The army's spirit rallied; they recovered Zhangpen Ford, took Xiao County, stormed White Tower, fought at Tushan, and brought five thousand captured civilians back to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而，侯進亡命駐靈璧，杜政、張興亦慮為北所害，窮窘自歸。

translations.literal: Before long Hou Jin was a fugitive stationed at Lingbi; Du Zheng and Zhang Xing also feared harm from the north and, in desperation, returned of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hou Jin was hiding at Lingbi, while Du Zheng and Zhang Xing, fearing the Mongols would kill them, came back in desperation.

sentences.zh: 益都撫而納之，興留徐，杜政還邳州。

translations.literal: Yidu comforted them and accepted them; Xing remained at Xu, and Du Zheng returned to Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu received and reassured them; Zhang Xing stayed at Xuzhou while Du Zheng went back to Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 益都資稟仁厚，持大體，二子兩侄為軍將，頗侵漁軍民。

translations.literal: Yidu was generous and magnanimous by nature and upheld the larger interest, but his two sons and two nephews were army officers and greatly preyed upon soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu was by nature humane and broad-minded, yet his sons and nephews in command posts plundered soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 青州人王祐為埽兵總領。

translations.literal: Wang You of Qingzhou was commander of the labor troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You of Qingzhou served as commander of the transport-labor troops.

sentences.zh: 將兵千七百人，益都常倚之，雖有過亦不責。

translations.literal: He commanded seventeen hundred troops; Yidu often relied on him and did not punish him even when he committed offenses.
translations.idiomatic: With seventeen hundred men under him, Yidu leaned on him heavily and overlooked his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 以故祐亦橫恣，與河間張祚、下邑令李閏、義勝都統封仙、遙授永州刺史成進忠輩，乘軍政廢弛，城中空虛。

translations.literal: For this reason You also acted with arrogant license; with Zhang Zuo of Hejian, Magistrate Li Run of Xiayi, Yisheng commander Feng Xian, and Acting Prefect Cheng Jinzhong of Yongzhou, taking advantage of lax military government and an empty city.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by Yidu's indulgence, You grew tyrannical; together with Zhang Zuo, Li Run, Feng Xian, Cheng Jinzhong, and others he exploited slack discipline and the city's weakness.

sentences.zh: 以六月丁巳夜燒草場作亂。

translations.literal: On the night of dingsi in the sixth month they burned the fodder yard and rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of dingsi in the sixth month they set the fodder depot ablaze and mutinied.

sentences.zh: 時張興臥病，祐恐事不成，起興與同行。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Xing lay ill; You feared the affair would fail, so he roused Xing to go with them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing was bedridden; fearing failure, You forced him to join the rising.

sentences.zh: 益都疑左右皆叛，挈妻子縋城而出，就從宜眾僧奴及東面總領劉安國軍。

translations.literal: Yidu suspected all around him had rebelled; he took his wife and children and let themselves down from the wall by rope, then joined Congyin Zhongsengnu and the army of Eastern commander Liu Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his entire staff had turned, Yidu lowered his family over the wall by rope and fled to Zhongsengnu and Liu Anguo's eastern command.

sentences.zh: 張興推祐為都元帥，複懼祐圖己，遂誅祐，並張祚殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xing made You supreme commander, then, fearing You plotted against him, executed You and also killed Zhang Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing proclaimed You supreme commander, then, fearing betrayal, killed You and Zhang Zuo alike.

sentences.zh: 因大掠城中。

translations.literal: They then plundered the city on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers then looted the city wholesale.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，國用安以行山東路尚書省事率兵至徐，張興率甲士迎之。

translations.literal: On renxu Guo Yong'an, acting as Shandong route minister, led troops to Xu; Zhang Xing led armored men to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Guo Yong'an arrived at Xuzhou as acting Shandong minister; Zhang Xing went out with armored troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: 用安輕騎而入，執興與其党十餘人，斬之於市，遂以封仙為元帥，兼節度使，主徐州。

translations.literal: Yong'an entered on light horse, seized Xing and more than ten of his partisans, and beheaded them in the market; he then made Feng Xian commander and concurrent military commissioner to govern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an rode in lightly, arrested Xing and a dozen conspirators, and executed them publicly; he installed Feng Xian as commander and commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 益都窘無所歸，乃奔宿州，節度使紇石烈阿虎以益都為人所逐不納，乃與諸將駐于城南。

translations.literal: Yidu, desperate with nowhere to go, fled to Suzhou; the military commissioner Heshenlie Ahu refused to admit him because he had been driven out, so he camped south of the city with his officers.
translations.idiomatic: Homeless, Yidu fled to Suzhou; Commissioner Heshenlie Ahu would not take him in, so he encamped south of the walls with his officers.

sentences.zh: 時宿之鎮防軍有逃還者，阿虎以為叛歸亦不納。

translations.literal: At that time some of Suzhou's garrison troops had fled and returned; Ahu regarded them as deserters coming back and would not admit them either.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzhou garrison men who had fled began drifting back, Ahu treated them as traitors and shut them out as well.

sentences.zh: 城中鎮防千戶高臘哥，結小吏郭仲安，謀就徐州將士內外相應以取宿，因歸楊妙真。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Gao Lage in the city joined petty official Guo Zhong'an to plot with Xuzhou officers for internal and external coordination to seize Suzhou and thereby submit to Yang Miaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city, garrison commander Gao Lage and clerk Guo Zhong'an plotted with Xuzhou commanders to open the gates and hand Suzhou to Yang Miaozhen.

sentences.zh: 甲戌夜半，開門納徐州總領王德全及妻弟高元哥軍。

translations.literal: At midnight on jiaxu they opened the gates and admitted the army of Xuzhou commander Wang Dequan and his brother-in-law Gao Yuange.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on jiaxu they opened the gates to Wang Dequan and Gao Yuange's troops.

sentences.zh: 劉安國尋亦入城，縛阿虎父子殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Anguo soon entered the city as well, bound Ahu and his son, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anguo then entered, seized Ahu and his son, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 州中請益都主帥府事，益都不從，曰：「吾國家舊人，為將帥亦久，以資性疏迂，不能周防，遂失重鎮。

translations.literal: The prefecture asked Yidu to head military affairs; Yidu refused, saying, "I am an old servant of our state and have long been a commander; because my nature is careless and slow, I could not take precautions in time and so lost a vital stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: The city asked Yidu to take command; he refused, saying, "I am an old Jin servant and long a general; my dull, careless nature cost us a great fortress.

sentences.zh: 今大事已去，方逃罪不暇，豈有改易髻發、奪人城池以降外方乎！

translations.literal: Now that the great cause is lost, I scarcely have time to flee punishment — how could I change my hairstyle and seize another's city to surrender to outsiders!"
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty is finished and I am fleeing for my life — I will not shave my head and seize cities to submit to outsiders!"

sentences.zh: 」即日，率官吏而行，至穀熟東，遇大兵，不屈而死。

translations.literal: " That same day he led the officials away; east of Gushu he met the great army and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: That day he led his staff away; east of Gushu he met Mongol troops and died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 徐州既歸海州，邳帥兀林答某亦讓印于杜政，遂送款于用安。

translations.literal: After Xuzhou submitted to Haizhou, Pizhou commander Wulinada Mou yielded his seal to Du Zheng and sent allegiance to Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou went over to Haizhou; the Pizhou commander surrendered his seal to Du Zheng, who then submitted to Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 已而宿州王德全、劉安國亦送款海州。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Dequan and Liu Anguo of Suzhou also sent allegiance to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Dequan and Liu Anguo of Suzhou did the same.

sentences.zh: 惟益都不改髻發，以至於死雲。

translations.literal: Only Yidu did not change his hairstyle, even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yidu kept his Jurchen queue to the end.

sentences.zh: 粘哥荊山

translations.literal: Nian Ge Jingshan
translations.idiomatic: Nian Ge Jingshan

sentences.zh: 粘哥荊山，不知其所始，正大中，累官亳州節度使。

translations.literal: Nian Ge Jingshan — his origins are unknown; in the Zhengda period he repeatedly held office and became military commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nian Ge Jingshan's origins are unrecorded; under Emperor Aizong's predecessor he rose to Bozhou military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年正月己丑，游騎自鄧至亳，鈔鹿邑，營于衛真西北五十里。

translations.literal: On jichou in the first month of the ninth year, roaming horsemen came from Deng to Bo, raided Luyi, and encamped fifty li northwest of Weizhen.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the first month of year nine, Mongol scouts from Deng reached Bozhou, raided Luyi, and camped northwest of Weizhen.

sentences.zh: 鹿邑令高昂霄知太康已降，即夜趨亳，道出衛真，呼縣令楚珩約同行。

translations.literal: Magistrate Gao Angxiao of Luyi, learning that Taikang had surrendered, hurried by night toward Bo; passing Weizhen he called Magistrate Chu Heng to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Luyi's magistrate Gao Angxiao, hearing Taikang had fallen, fled by night toward Bozhou and summoned Weizhen's Chu Heng to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 珩知勢不支，即明諭縣人以避遷之意，遂同走亳。

translations.literal: Heng knew resistance was impossible; he openly told the county people of the intent to flee relocation, and then they fled together to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Heng knew the position was hopeless; he told the county openly they must evacuate, then fled with Gao to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，二邑皆降。

translations.literal: On dingwei both counties surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei both counties surrendered.

sentences.zh: 是日，軍至亳州城下。

translations.literal: That day the army reached below Bozhou city.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Mongol army appeared before Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 州止有單州兵四百人，號「鎮安軍」，提控楊春、邢某、都統戴興屯已六年。

translations.literal: The prefecture had only four hundred troops from Danzhou, called the "Pacifying Army," under commanders Yang Chun, Xing Mou, and commander Dai Xing, stationed there six years.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou held only four hundred Danzhou troops, the "Pacifying Army," under Yang Chun, Xing, and Dai Xing, who had been posted there six years.

sentences.zh: 荊山悉籍城中丁壯為軍，修守具，而大兵亦不暇攻。

translations.literal: Jingshan enrolled all able-bodied men in the city as soldiers, repaired defenses, and the great army also had no leisure to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan conscripted every able man, repaired defenses, and the Mongols likewise did not press a full assault.

sentences.zh: 四月，擁降民而北，城門閉，不之知也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they drove relocated civilians northward; the city gates were closed, and they did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Mongols herded surrendered civilians north; the gates stayed shut and the garrison knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 五月，縱遷民收麥，老幼得出，丁壯悉留之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they allowed relocated people to harvest wheat; the old and young could leave, but all able-bodied men were detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month evacuees were allowed to harvest wheat — elders and children could leave, but every able-bodied man was held.

sentences.zh: 民往往不肯留而遁，數日，城為之空。

translations.literal: The people often refused to stay and fled; within days the city was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: People refused detention and slipped away until within days the city stood empty.

sentences.zh: 荊山遣將領各詣所屬招之，並將領亦不返。

translations.literal: Jingshan sent officers to their districts to summon them back, but the officers themselves also did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan sent officers to recall the men, but those officers never came back either.

sentences.zh: 「鎮安」者皆紅祆餘黨，力盡來歸，變詐反復，朝廷終以盜賊待之。

translations.literal: The "Pacifying Army" were all remnants of the Red Scarves; having exhausted their strength they came to submit, treacherous and changeable; the court always treated them as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifying Army were Red Turban holdouts — spent, treacherous, and always regarded by the court as bandits.

sentences.zh: 荊山以遷民為軍，蓋防之也。

translations.literal: Jingshan made the relocated people into an army — this was to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan drafted the evacuees into service chiefly to keep them under control.

sentences.zh: 及召外兵不至，乃請於歸德，得甲騎百餘，兩總領統之。

translations.literal: When summoned outside troops did not arrive, he requested from Guide and obtained a little over a hundred armored horsemen, commanded by two chief officers.
translations.idiomatic: With outside reinforcements failing, he begged Guide for a hundred-odd cavalry under two commanders.

sentences.zh: 既至，「鎮安」疑其謀己，乃乘將士新到不設備，至夜，掩殺殆盡。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the Pacifying Army suspected a plot against them; taking advantage of the newcomers' lack of precautions on arrival, at night they ambushed and killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifying Army feared a plot; that night, while the newcomers were off guard, they ambushed and slaughtered almost the entire detachment.

sentences.zh: 荊山出走衛真，楚珩與之馬而去，州中豪貴悉被剽略。

translations.literal: Jingshan fled to Weizhen; Chu Heng gave him a horse and left; the city's wealthy and eminent were all plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan fled to Weizhen; Chu Heng gave him a horse and escaped; Bozhou's elite were looted clean.

sentences.zh: 劉堅者，初為大兵守城父，亳州複，擒之，囚之於獄。

translations.literal: Liu Jian had first guarded Chengfù for the great army; when Bozhou was recovered, he was captured and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian had once held Chengfù for the Mongols; when Bozhou was retaken, he was captured and jailed.

sentences.zh: 楊春謀欲北降，乃出之，使為宣差。

translations.literal: Yang Chun plotted to surrender northward, so released him and made him an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun, planning to defect north, released him and appointed him envoy.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大兵石總管入州，改州為順天府，春為總管，戴興為同知，劉順治中，留党項軍千人戍之。

translations.literal: On yisi the great army's Commissioner Shi entered the prefecture, changed the prefecture to Shuntian Prefecture; Chun became commissioner, Dai Xing vice commissioner, Liu Shun administrative aide; a thousand Tangut troops were left to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Mongol Commissioner Shi took the city, renamed it Shuntian Prefecture, installed Yang Chun and Dai Xing, and left a thousand Tangut guards.

sentences.zh: 屬縣皆下，惟城父令李用宜不降，其妻子在亳，春以為質，竟不屈而死。

translations.literal: Subordinate counties all submitted; only Magistrate Li Yongyi of Chengfù did not surrender; his wife and children were in Bo — Chun held them hostage, yet he still would not yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Every subordinate county submitted except Chengfù's Li Yongyi; though Chun held his family hostage in Bozhou, he refused to yield and was killed.

sentences.zh: 春既據州，與劉堅坐樓上，召副提控邢某。

translations.literal: Chun having seized the prefecture, he and Liu Jian sat in a tower and summoned Vice Commander Xing Mou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Chun held Bozhou, he and Liu Jian sat in a tower and sent for Vice Commander Xing.

sentences.zh: 邢剛直循理，將士嚴憚之，時臥病，聞春亂，流涕不自禁。

translations.literal: Xing was upright and followed principle; officers and soldiers greatly feared him; he lay ill at the time; hearing of Chun's disorder, he wept uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was rigidly upright and feared by the troops; bedridden, he wept uncontrollably when he heard of Chun's treason.

sentences.zh: 春遣人舁致之，邢指春大罵，春慚恧無言。

translations.literal: Chun sent men to carry him there; Xing pointed at Chun and cursed him loudly; Chun was ashamed and speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had him carried in; Xing cursed him to his face while Chun stood mute with shame.

sentences.zh: 春欲殺荊山家，邢力勸止之，且令給道路費送之出城，邢尋病卒。

translations.literal: Chun wished to kill Jingshan's family; Xing strongly urged him to stop and also ordered travel expenses to send them out of the city; Xing soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Chun meant to massacre Jingshan's household; Xing stopped him and paid their passage out of the city; Xing soon died.

sentences.zh: 二年夏四月，北省忒木泬攻歸德，春以戴興提精卒以往，獨與疲弱者守城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second summer year, the northern province's Temüge attacked Guide; Chun sent Dai Xing with elite troops while he alone guarded the city with the weak.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year two, Temüge of the northern command attacked Guide; Chun sent Dai Xing with elites while he stayed with the weak.

sentences.zh: 州人王賓遂反正，春渡河北遁。

translations.literal: The prefecture's Wang Bin then restored allegiance to Jin; Chun fled north across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin of Bozhou restored Jin rule; Yang Chun fled north across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 既而崔七斤為亂，殺王賓。

translations.literal: Before long Cui Qijin made disorder and killed Wang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cui Qijin mutinied and killed Wang Bin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不得已，以七斤為節度使，就其兵仗入蔡。

translations.literal: The court, having no choice, made Qijin military commissioner and took his arms into Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The court, helpless, made Qijin commissioner and marched his troops to Cai.

sentences.zh: 八月，劉順攻亳州，破之，七斤為城父令所殺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Liu Shun attacked Bozhou, broke it, and Qijin was killed by the Chengfù magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Shun retook Bozhou; Qijin was killed by Chengfù's magistrate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，單州軍以州人殺其家屬，召大兵來攻，蚧能拔，殺屬縣民而去。

translations.literal: Before long Danzhou troops, because locals had killed their families, summoned the great army to attack; after a long siege they withdrew, killing people of subordinate counties as they left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Danzhou troops, whose families had been killed locally, called in the Mongols; after a long siege they withdrew, massacring county populations.

sentences.zh: 既渡河，知亳人不疑，複來攻，州竟為春所破。

translations.literal: Having crossed the river and knowing the people of Bo were off guard, they came again to attack, and the prefecture was finally broken by Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing back, they found Bozhou unwary, attacked again, and Yang Chun finally took the city.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，宋人來攻，春出降，劉堅北走。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year the Song came to attack; Chun surrendered, and Liu Jian fled north.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month the Song attacked; Chun surrendered and Liu Jian fled north.

sentences.zh: 附:劉均

translations.literal: Appendix: Liu Jun
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Liu Jun

sentences.zh: 劉均者，林慮人，時為亳州觀察判官。

translations.literal: Liu Jun was a man of Linyu and at the time served as Bozhou administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Linyu was then Bozhou's administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 春既逐荊山，納款大兵，脅均同降。

translations.literal: Chun having driven out Jingshan and submitted to the great army, he coerced Jun to surrender with him.
translations.idiomatic: After driving out Jingshan and submitting to the Mongols, Yang Chun forced Jun to join him.

sentences.zh: 均佯應之，歸其家取朝服服之， 顧謂妻子曰：「我起身刀筆，仰荷上知，始列朝著，又佐大籓，死亦足矣。

translations.literal: Jun pretended to agree, went home to put on court robes, and turning to his wife said, "I rose from clerk's work, owed to the emperor's favor I first entered court dress and then assisted a great fan — death is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Jun feigned consent, donned court robes at home, and told his wife, "I began as a clerk, was raised to court rank and a great commission — I have lived enough.

sentences.zh: 今頭顱已如此，假使有十年壽，何以見先帝於地下乎。

translations.literal: Now my head is already like this; even if I had ten years of life, how could I face the late emperor underground?
translations.idiomatic: My head is already forfeit; even ten more years could not let me face our late emperor in the grave."

sentences.zh: 」即仰藥而死。

translations.literal: " He immediately took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 王賓，字德卿，亳州人。

translations.literal: Wang Bin, style Deqing, was a man of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin, courtesy name Deqing, was a native of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Zhenyou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhenyou 2 (1214).

sentences.zh: 外若曠達，而深有謀畫。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed free and easy, yet inwardly he was deeply resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: He seemed easygoing in manner but was deeply calculating.

sentences.zh: 初調蘭陵主簿，辟虹縣令，尋入為尚書省令史，坐事罷歸鄉里。

translations.literal: At first appointed Lanling registrar, then summoned as Hong county magistrate; soon he entered the Ministry of Revenue as a clerk, was dismissed for an offense, and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Lanling registrar, then Hong county magistrate, then a Ministry clerk until dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 天興元年正月，亳州軍變，節度使粘哥荊山出走，楊春以州出降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tianxing, the Bozhou army mutinied; Military Commissioner Nian Ge Jingshan fled; Yang Chun surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing 1's first month the Bozhou garrison mutinied; Jingshan fled and Yang Chun surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 既而，自以羸兵守之。

translations.literal: Before long he himself guarded it with weak troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then held the city with only a weak remnant force.

sentences.zh: 賓與前譙縣尉王進、魏節亨、呂鈞約城中軍民複其州，楊春遂遁，遣節亨詣歸德以聞。

translations.literal: Bin with former Qiao county captain Wang Jin, Wei Jieheng, and Lü Jun plotted with soldiers and civilians in the city to recover the prefecture; Yang Chun fled; they sent Jieheng to Guide to report.
translations.idiomatic: Bin joined Wang Jin, Wei Jieheng, and Lü Jun to rally the city, drive off Yang Chun, and send Jieheng to Guide with the news.

sentences.zh: 哀宗嘉之，授進節度使，賓同知節度使，節亨節度副使，鈞觀察判官。

translations.literal: The Aizong Emperor was pleased and appointed Jin military commissioner, Bin vice commissioner, Jieheng deputy commissioner, and Jun administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong rewarded them: Jin as commissioner, Bin as vice commissioner, Jieheng as deputy, Jun as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 楊春複以兵來攻，月餘不能拔，即渡河而北。

translations.literal: Yang Chun again came with troops to attack; for more than a month he could not take it, then crossed the river north.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun attacked again for over a month, failed, and retreated north across the river.

sentences.zh: 六月，哀宗遷蔡，賓奉迎於州北之高安。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Aizong Emperor moved to Cai; Bin went to welcome him at Gao'an north of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, as the emperor moved to Cai, Bin welcomed him at Gao'an north of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 上與語，大悅，恨用之晚，擢為行部尚書、世襲謀克。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke with him and was greatly pleased, regretting he had been used late; he was promoted to Minister of the Travelling Secretariat and hereditary mouke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in him, lamented his late discovery, and made him Travelling Minister and hereditary mouke.

sentences.zh: 上初至亳，賓等適征民丁負鐵甲入蔡，及會計忠孝軍家屬口糧，故留參知政事張天綱董之，就遷有功將士。

translations.literal: When the emperor first reached Bo, Bin and others happened to be conscripting men to carry iron armor to Cai and tallying grain for Zhongxiao Army families, so Participating Minister Zhang Tiangang was left to oversee it and promote meritorious officers.
translations.idiomatic: When the court reached Bozhou, Bin was conscripting porters for Cai and rationing Zhongxiao dependents; Zhang Tiangang was left to manage promotions.

sentences.zh: 時亳之糧儲不廣，賓等常吝惜，軍士以此歸怨。

translations.literal: At that time Bozhou's grain stores were not ample; Bin and others were often stingy, and for this the soldiers bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou's stores were thin; Bin's frugality bred deep resentment among the troops.

sentences.zh: 及運甲之役，複不欲行。

translations.literal: When the task of transporting armor came, they again did not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: When orders came to haul armor to Cai, the men refused to march.

sentences.zh: 會天綱與賓等於一樓上銓次立功等第，鎮防軍崔複哥、王六十之徒擐甲嘩噪登樓，天綱問曰：「即欲見殺，容我望闕拜辭。

translations.literal: When Tiangang met Bin and others on a tower to rank merit grades, Cui Fuge, Wang Liushi, and others in armor clamored up the tower; Tiangang asked, "If you mean to kill me, allow me to bow toward the palace to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: As Tiangang ranked merit on a tower, Cui Fuge and Wang Liushi stormed up in armor; Tiangang asked only to bow toward the palace before dying.

sentences.zh: 」賊曰：「無預相公。

translations.literal: " The rebels said, "It does not concern the minister.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers said, "Not you, minister."

sentences.zh: 」即拽賓及呂鈞往市中。

translations.literal: " They immediately dragged Bin and Lü Jun to the market.
translations.idiomatic: They dragged Bin and Lü Jun into the street.

sentences.zh: 鈞且行且跪，涕淚俱下。

translations.literal: Jun went along kneeling as he walked, tears streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jun crawled along, weeping as he went.

sentences.zh: 賓岸然不懼，大叫曰：「不過殺我。

translations.literal: Bin stood unafraid and shouted, "You can only kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Bin stood erect and cried, "Kill me if you will."

sentences.zh: 但殺，但殺！

translations.literal: Just kill, just kill!
translations.idiomatic: Kill me — kill me!"

sentences.zh: 」乃並害之。

translations.literal: " They then killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: They murdered them both.

sentences.zh: 節度副使魏節亨、節度判官孫良、觀察副使孫九住皆被害。

translations.literal: Deputy Commissioner Wei Jieheng, Commissioner Aide Sun Liang, and Vice Administrative Aide Sun Jiuzhu were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commissioner Wei Jieheng, aide Sun Liang, and vice aide Sun Jiuzhu were slain as well.

sentences.zh: 又數日，殺節度使王進。

translations.literal: Several days later they killed Military Commissioner Wang Jin.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the mutineers killed Commissioner Wang Jin.

sentences.zh: 進嘗應荊山之募，由間道入汴京納奏，賞以物不受，又散家所有濟貧民，以死自勵。

translations.literal: Jin had once answered Jingshan's recruitment, entered the capital by secret path to deliver memorials, refused rewards of goods, and also distributed all his household property to aid the poor, taking death as his spur.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had entered Bianjing by a secret route with Jingshan's summons, refused imperial gifts, gave his wealth to the poor, and held himself ready to die.

sentences.zh: 至汴，以勞遷本州節度判官。

translations.literal: Reaching Bian, he was transferred for merit to administrative aide of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he was promoted to Bozhou administrative aide for his service.

sentences.zh: 賜以白金，亦不受，一時甚稱之。

translations.literal: Granted white silver, he also refused it; for a time he was greatly praised.
translations.idiomatic: Even offered silver he would not take it, and for a time won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 附:王進 等

translations.literal: Appendix: Wang Jin and others
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Wang Jin and others

sentences.zh: 有李喜住者，本宿州眾僧奴下宣差。

translations.literal: There was one Li Xizhu, originally an envoy under Zhongsengnu of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: One Li Xizhu had served as an envoy under Suzhou's Zhongsengnu.

sentences.zh: 天興二年四月，進糧入歸德，將還，聞亳州王進反正，制旨以喜住為振武都尉，將兵三千應援。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Tianxing, bringing grain into Guide and about to return, he heard Wang Jin of Bozhou had restored allegiance; an edict made Xizhu Pacifying Martial Commandant with three thousand troops to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing 2's fourth month, while hauling grain to Guide, he learned Jin had restored Bozhou; the court named him Pacifying Martial Commandant with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是時，太赤圍亳步騎十萬，喜住以眾寡不敵，獨與三人間道入城，王進方議遷左軍林，喜住不可，進即以兵付喜住。

translations.literal: At that time Taichi besieged Bo with a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry; Xizhu, unable to match their numbers, entered the city by secret path with only three men; Jin was discussing moving to Zuojunlin — Xizhu objected, and Jin handed the troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Taichi had a hundred thousand men around Bozhou; Xizhu slipped in with three companions while Jin was debating evacuation — Xizhu refused, and Jin gave him the army.

sentences.zh: 大兵攻八日不能下。

translations.literal: The great army attacked eight days and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols assaulted the city eight days without success.

sentences.zh: 五月壬子，兵退。

translations.literal: On renzi in the fifth month the troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the fifth month the besiegers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 己未，官奴與阿裏合提忠孝軍百人至亳，與諸將議遷可否。

translations.literal: On jiwei Guannu and Aligeti's Zhongxiao Army of a hundred men reached Bo and discussed with the generals whether relocation was feasible.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Guannu and Aligeti arrived with a hundred Zhongxiao troops to debate moving the court.

sentences.zh: 以為不可，當留輜重于蔡，選軍扈從入聖朵就武仙軍，遂入關中。

translations.literal: They held it impossible; baggage should be left at Cai, select troops to escort the emperor into Shengdou to join Wuxian's army, then enter Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: They argued the court should leave stores at Cai, march into Shengdou to join Wuxian, and withdraw into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 關中地利可恃，又有郭蝦蟆等軍在西可恃。

translations.literal: Guanzhong's terrain could be relied upon, and there were also Guo Xiamo's troops in the west to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong offered defensible ground and Guo Xiamo's forces in the west.

sentences.zh: 五月甲子，召官奴還歸德，不赴，再召，留其軍半於亳乃赴。

translations.literal: On jiazi in the fifth month Guannu was summoned back to Guide but did not go; summoned again, he left half his army at Bo and then went.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned twice to Guide, Guannu kept half his force at Bozhou before obeying.

sentences.zh: 六月壬辰，車駕舟行至亳，王進奏：「臣本軍伍，不知治體，如李喜住扈從入蔡，則毫不守矣。

translations.literal: On renchen in the sixth month the imperial carriage arrived at Bo by boat; Wang Jin memorialized, "Your servant is of the military ranks and does not understand governance; if Li Xizhu escorts you to Cai, this prefecture will be utterly undefended.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor reached Bozhou by boat; Jin pleaded, "I am a soldier, not an administrator — if Xizhu follows Your Majesty to Cai, Bozhou will be left empty."

sentences.zh: 乞留治此州。

translations.literal: I beg to remain and govern this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Let me stay and hold this prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」詔以喜住為集慶軍節度使，便宜從事，進領帥職。

translations.literal: " An edict made Xizhu Jiqing Army military commissioner with discretionary authority; Jin took the chief command.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Xizhu Jiqing commissioner with full discretion while Jin retained supreme command.

sentences.zh: 七月，進死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jin died.

sentences.zh: 喜住先往城父督糧餫，聞亂遂不敢入亳，後投宋。

translations.literal: Xizhu had first gone to Chengfù to supervise grain transport; hearing of the disorder he dared not enter Bo and later went over to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhu, away at Chengfù procuring grain, dared not return after the mutiny and eventually defected to Song.

sentences.zh: 論曰：金季之亂，軍士欲代其偏裨，偏裨欲代其主將，即群起而僨之。

translations.literal: Commentary says: In the disorder of late Jin, soldiers wished to replace their platoon leaders, platoon leaders wished to replace their commanders — they would rise together and overthrow them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary notes that in Jin's final chaos soldiers overthrew platoon leaders and platoon leaders overthrew generals without restraint.

sentences.zh: 無複忌憚。

translations.literal: There was no further scruple.
translations.idiomatic: No one hesitated any longer.

sentences.zh: 益都、荊山皆忠亮之士，賓、進才略尤足取焉，而並不免於難，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yidu and Jingshan were both loyal and upright men; Bin and Jin's talent and strategy were especially admirable, yet none escaped calamity — how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Yidu and Jingshan were loyal; Bin and Jin were gifted — yet all perished, a bitter loss.

sentences.zh: 國用安

translations.literal: Guo Yong'an
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong'an

sentences.zh: 國用安，先名安用，本名咬兒，淄州人。

translations.literal: Guo Yong'an — formerly named An Yong, original name Yao'er, a man of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong'an — born An Yong, nicknamed Bite-er, from Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 紅祆賊楊安兒、李全餘黨也。

translations.literal: He was a remnant of the Red Scarves Yang An'er and Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a follower of the Red Turban leaders Yang An'er and Li Quan.

sentences.zh: 嘗歸順大元，為都元帥、行山東路尚書省事。

translations.literal: He had once submitted to the Great Yuan and become supreme commander and acting Shandong route minister.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted to the Mongols as supreme commander and Shandong minister.

sentences.zh: 天興元年六月，徐州埽兵總領王祐、義勝軍都統封仙、總領張興等夜燒草場作亂，逐元帥徒單益都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianxing, Wang You, commander of Xuzhou labor troops, Feng Xian of the Yisheng Army, Zhang Xing and others burned the fodder yard by night and rebelled, driving out Commander Tudan Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing 1's sixth month Wang You, Feng Xian, and Zhang Xing mutinied at Xuzhou and expelled Yidu.

sentences.zh: 安用率兵入徐，執張興與其党十餘人斬之，以封仙為元帥兼節度使，主徐州。

translations.literal: An Yong led troops into Xu, seized Zhang Xing and more than ten partisans and beheaded them, made Feng Xian commander and concurrent commissioner, and governed Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Yong entered Xuzhou, executed Zhang Xing's faction, and installed Feng Xian as commander.

sentences.zh: 宿州鎮防軍千戶高臘哥與東面總帥劉安國構徐州總帥王德全，殺宿帥紇石烈阿虎，以其州歸海州。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Gao Lage of Suzhou and Eastern commander Liu Anguo colluded with Xuzhou commander Wang Dequan, killed Commissioner Heshenlie Ahu, and gave the prefecture to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lage and Liu Anguo killed Suzhou's commissioner and handed the city to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 邳州從宜兀林答某亦讓州于杜政，送款海州。

translations.literal: Pizhou acting commander Wulinada Mou also yielded the prefecture to Du Zheng and sent allegiance to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pizhou's acting commander surrendered to Du Zheng and Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而皆歸安用。

translations.literal: Before long all submitted to An Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all fell under An Yong.

sentences.zh: 北大將阿術魯聞安用據徐、宿、邳，大怒曰：「此三州我當攻取，安用何人，輒受降。

translations.literal: The northern great general Ashulu, hearing An Yong held Xu, Su, and Pi, said in great anger, "These three prefectures I ought to take — who is An Yong to accept their surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: Mongol general Ashulu raged that An Yong had accepted Xu, Suzhou, and Pizhou — "I was to take those cities — who is this man?"

sentences.zh: 」遣信安、張進等率兵入徐，欲圖安用，奪其軍。

translations.literal: " He sent Xin'an, Zhang Jin, and others to lead troops into Xu, intending to plot against An Yong and seize his army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Jin into Xuzhou to destroy An Yong and seize his troops.

sentences.zh: 安用懼，謀于德全，劫殺張進及海州元帥田福等數百人，與楊妙真絕，乃還邳州。

translations.literal: An Yong was afraid; he plotted with Dequan, waylaid and killed Zhang Jin and Haizhou commander Tian Fu and several hundred others, broke with Yang Miaozhen, and returned to Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Ashulu, he murdered Zhang Jin and Tian Fu, broke with Yang Miaozhen, and retreated to Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 會山東諸將及徐、宿、邳主帥，刑馬結盟，誓歸金朝。

translations.literal: He met Shandong generals and the commanders of Xu, Su, and Pi, cut a horse and formed an alliance, swearing to return to the Jin court.
translations.idiomatic: He met Shandong commanders, sacrificed a horse, and swore allegiance back to Jin.

sentences.zh: 既盟，諸將皆散去，安用無所歸，遂同德全、安國托從宜眾僧奴自通於朝廷。

translations.literal: After the alliance the generals all dispersed; An Yong had nowhere to go, so with Dequan and Anguo he had Zhongsengnu communicate with the court on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When the allies dispersed, he had Zhongsengnu petition the Jin court for him.

sentences.zh: 眾僧奴遣人上奏：「安用以數州反正，功甚大。

translations.literal: Zhongsengnu sent a memorial up: "An Yong has restored several prefectures — the merit is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsengnu wrote, "An Yong's restoration of several prefectures is a great service."

sentences.zh: 且其兵力強盛，材略可稱。

translations.literal: Moreover his military strength is formidable and his talent and strategy commendable.
translations.idiomatic: His troops are strong and his talent proven."

sentences.zh: 國家果欲倚用，非極品重權不足以堅其許國之心。

translations.literal: If the state truly wishes to rely on him, nothing short of the highest rank and weighty authority will suffice to firm his heart in pledging to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Only the highest rank will bind his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」未報。

translations.literal: " No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 安用率兵萬人攻海州，未至，眾稍散去。

translations.literal: An Yong led ten thousand troops to attack Haizhou; before arriving, the force gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He marched ten thousand men on Haizhou, but they melted away before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 安國因勸安用當赤心歸國，安用亦自知反復失計，事已無可奈何，於是複金朝衣冠。

translations.literal: Anguo therefore urged An Yong to devote his heart to the state; An Yong also knew himself changeable and mistaken, the affair already beyond remedy, and so resumed Jin court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo persuaded him to return wholeheartedly; knowing his schemes had failed, An Yong donned Jin dress again.

sentences.zh: 妙真怒其叛己，又懼為所圖，悉屠安用家走益都。

translations.literal: Miaozhen was angry he had betrayed her and feared being plotted against; she slaughtered all An Yong's family and fled to Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Miaozhen massacred his household and fled to Yidu.

sentences.zh: 安用遂選兵分將，期必得妙真，自此淮海之上無寧歲矣。

translations.literal: An Yong then selected troops and divided commanders, determined to get Miaozhen; from this there was no peaceful year on the Huai-Hai.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted Miaozhen relentlessly, and the Huai-Hai knew no peace thereafter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，朝廷遣近侍局直長因世英、都事高天祐持手詔至邳，以安用為開府儀同三司、平章政事、兼都元帥、京東山東等路行尚書省事，特封兗王，賜號「英烈戡難保節忠臣」，錫姓完顏，附屬籍，改名用安，賜金鍍銀印、駝紐金印、金虎符、世襲千戶宣命、敕樣、牌樣、禦畫體宣、空頭河朔山東赦文，便宜從事，且以彭王妃誥委用安招妙真。

translations.literal: Before long the court sent Inner Service Director Yin Shiying and Secretariat officer Gao Tianyou with a handwritten edict to Pi, making An Yong Grand Mentor of the State, Grand Councillor, concurrent supreme commander and Eastern-Shandong route minister, specially enfeoffed Prince of Yan, granted the title "Heroic Martyr Who Quells Disaster and Preserves Integrity and Loyalty," bestowed the surname Wanyan, attached to the registry, renamed Yong'an, granted gold-plated silver seal, camel-knob gold seal, gold tiger tally, hereditary thousand-household commission, edict models, plaque models, imperial-painted rescript, blank amnesty for Hebei-Shandong, discretionary authority, and also entrusted the Princess of Peng's patent to Yong'an to recruit Miaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Yin Shiying with a handwritten edict enfeoffing him Prince of Yan, renaming him Guo Yong'an with Wanyan surname and lavish seals, and tasked him to win over Miaozhen.

sentences.zh: 用安始聞使者至，猶豫未決，以總領楊懋迎使者入，監於州廨，問所以來。

translations.literal: When Yong'an first heard envoys had come he hesitated; Chief Yang Mao welcomed the envoys in, detained them at the prefectural office, and asked their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an hesitated until Yang Mao brought the envoys in under guard and questioned them.

sentences.zh: 世英對以封建事，意頗順。

translations.literal: Shiying answered regarding the enfeoffment; his manner was rather compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying spoke of the enfeoffment and seemed agreeable.

sentences.zh: 諸帥王、杜輩皆不欲宣言，欲殺使者。

translations.literal: The commanders Wang, Du, and others all did not wish to proclaim it and wanted to kill the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, Du, and other warlords wanted the envoys killed.

sentences.zh: 明日，用安乃出見使者，跪揖如等夷。

translations.literal: The next day Yong'an came out to see the envoys and knelt and bowed as to an equal.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he met them and bowed as to peers.

sentences.zh: 坐定，語世英曰：「予向隨大兵攻汴，嘗于開陽門下與侯摯議內外夾擊。

translations.literal: When seated he said to Shiying, "I once followed the great army attacking Bian and at Kaiyang Gate discussed with Hou Zhi a coordinated strike inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Seated, he told Shiying he had once urged Hou Zhi to strike Bian from within and without at Kaiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 此時大兵病死者眾，十七頭項皆在京城，若從吾計出軍，中興久矣。

translations.literal: At that time many of the great army died of illness; the seventeen commanders were all in the capital — if they had followed my plan and sent out troops, restoration would have been achieved long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Had the seventeen Mongol commanders in Bian followed his plan, Jin might have revived long before.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃無一人敢決者，今日悔將何及。

translations.literal: Yet the court had not a single man who dared decide; today what is the use of regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no one at court dared act — now regret was useless.

sentences.zh: 」言竟而起。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking he rose.
translations.idiomatic: He rose when he finished.

sentences.zh: 既而選人取朝廷賜物遍觀之，喜見顏色。

translations.literal: Before long he selected men to take the court's gifts and view them all; joy showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he had the imperial gifts displayed and brightened at the sight.

sentences.zh: 複與使者私議，欲不以朝禮受之，世英等不可，即設宴拜授如儀，以主事常謹等隨使者奉表入謝。

translations.literal: He again privately discussed with the envoys, wishing not to receive them by court ritual; Shiying and others would not agree; they then set a banquet and invested him by ritual; Clerk Chang Jin and others followed the envoys to present a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to avoid court ceremony; the envoys insisted; after a banquet he accepted, and Chang Jin went to court with thanks.

sentences.zh: 上複遺世英、天祐賜以鐵券一、虎符六、龍文衣一、玉魚帶一、弓矢二、封贈其父母妻誥命，及郡王宣、世襲宣、大信牌、玉兔鶻帶各十，聽同盟可賜者賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Shiying and Tianyou with an iron certificate, six tiger tallies, one dragon-pattern robe, one jade-fish belt, two bows and arrows, patents ennobling his parents and wife, and ten each of prince patents, hereditary patents, great-trust plaques, and jade-hawk belts — whomever among allies might be granted, grant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added an iron certificate, tallies, robes, belts, bows, ennoblements, and patents for allies.

sentences.zh: 使者至邳，用安迎受如禮，始有入援意。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached Pi, Yong'an received them by ritual and first had the intention to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: At Pi he received them properly and began to consider marching to aid the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及聞上將遷蔡州，乃遣人以蠟書言遷蔡有六不可，大率以謂：「歸德環城皆水，卒難攻擊，蔡無此險，一也。

translations.literal: When he heard the emperor would move to Caizhou, he sent a wax-sealed letter saying there were six reasons moving to Cai was inadvisable, generally stating, "Guide is surrounded by water on all sides and hard to assault at once; Cai lacks this advantage — first.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the move to Cai, he sent a wax letter listing six objections, first that Guide's moats were safer than Cai's.

sentences.zh: 歸德雖乏糧儲，而魚芡可以取足，蔡若受圍，廩食有限，二也。

translations.literal: Guide though lacking grain stores can be supplied with fish and water plants; if Cai is besieged, granary food is limited — second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Guide could still feed itself from rivers; besieged Cai could not.

sentences.zh: 大兵所以去歸德者，非畏我也，縱之出而躡其後，舍其難而就其易者攻焉，三也。

translations.literal: The reason the great army left Guide was not fear of us; they let us out and trailed behind, abandoning the difficult to attack the easy — third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Mongols were luring the court from a defensible city to an easy target.

sentences.zh: 蔡去宋境不百里，萬一資敵兵糧，禍不可解，四也。

translations.literal: Cai is not a hundred li from Song territory; if by chance it supplies enemy troops and grain, disaster cannot be undone — fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, Cai lay within a hundred li of Song territory and might feed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 歸德不保，水道東行猶可以去，蔡若不守，去將安之，五也。

translations.literal: If Guide cannot be held, going east by waterway can still be done; if Cai is not held, where will you go — fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, if Guide fell one could still flee east by water; from Cai there was no escape.

sentences.zh: 時方暑雨，千里泥淖，聖體豐澤，不便鞍馬，倉卒遇敵，非臣子所敢言，六也。

translations.literal: It is just the season of summer rains; a thousand li of mire; the sacred person is well nourished and unfit for horseback; meeting the enemy in haste — not what subjects dare speak of — sixth.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, summer rains and mud made flight dangerous for the emperor's person — a subject dared not say more.

sentences.zh: 雖然，陛下必欲去歸德，莫如權幸山東。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, if Your Majesty must leave Guide, nothing is better than temporarily visiting Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Still, if the emperor must leave Guide, he should visit Shandong first.

sentences.zh: 山東富庶甲天下，臣略有其地，東連沂、海，西接徐、邳，南扼盱、楚，北控淄、齊。

translations.literal: Shandong's wealth tops the realm; I roughly hold its territory — east connecting Yi and Hai, west joining Xu and Pi, south blocking Chu and Xuyi, north controlling Zi and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong was the richest region; he held lands from Yi to the sea, Xu to Pi, Huai to Qi.

sentences.zh: 若鑾輿少停，臣仰賴威靈，河朔之地可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage pauses briefly, relying on your majesty's majesty I can take Hebei with a proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor paused there, he could recover Hebei by proclamation.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下審察。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: He begged the emperor to consider it.

sentences.zh: 」上以其言示宰臣。

translations.literal: " The emperor showed his words to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the letter to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏用安反復，本無匡輔志，此必參議張介等議之，業已遷蔡，議遂寢。

translations.literal: The chief ministers memorialized that Yong'an was changeable and originally had no mind to assist; this must have been discussed by Participating Councillor Zhang Jie and others; the move to Cai was already done, and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers said Yong'an was treacherous and the plan, likely Zhang Jie's, was ignored once the move to Cai began.

sentences.zh: 初，世英等過徐，王德全、劉安國說之曰：「朝廷恩命豈宜出自用安，郡王宣吾二人最當得者，乞就留之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shiying and others passed Xu, Wang Dequan and Liu Anguo said to them, "Court favor ought not to come from Yong'an; the prince patents — we two should most receive them; we beg you leave them here.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xuzhou, Dequan and Anguo demanded the prince patents meant for them, not Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 」世英乃留郡王宣、世襲宣、玉帶各二。

translations.literal: " Shiying then left two each of prince patent, hereditary patent, and jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying left two of each.

sentences.zh: 由是與用安有隙，又懼為所圖，皆不聽其節制。

translations.literal: For this they had a rift with Yong'an and also feared being plotted against; both refused his command.
translations.idiomatic: They feuded with Yong'an and ignored his orders.

sentences.zh: 十郡王者，李明德、封仙、張瑀、張友、卓翼、康琮、杜政、吳歪頭、王德全、劉安國也。

translations.literal: The ten prefectural kings were Li Mingde, Feng Xian, Zhang Yu, Zhang You, Zhuo Yi, Kang Cong, Du Zheng, Wu Wai'tou, Wang Dequan, and Liu Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Ten warlords — Li Mingde, Feng Xian, Zhang Yu, Zhang You, Zhuo Yi, Kang Cong, Du Zheng, Wu Wai'tou, Dequan, and Anguo — ruled their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 用安必欲取山東，累征徐、宿兵，止以勤王為辭，二帥不應。

translations.literal: Yong'an was determined to take Shandong and repeatedly summoned Xu and Su troops, using aiding the emperor only as a pretext; the two commanders did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an repeatedly demanded Xu and Su troops under the pretense of relieving the emperor; both refused.

sentences.zh: 用安怒，令杜政等率兵三千，以取糧為名，襲徐、宿。

translations.literal: Yong'an was angry and ordered Du Zheng and others to lead three thousand troops, under the name of gathering grain, to raid Xu and Su.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Du Zheng with three thousand men to seize grain — in truth to attack Xu and Su.

sentences.zh: 既入城，德全覺之，就留杜政、封仙不遣。

translations.literal: Having entered the city, Dequan perceived it and detained Du Zheng and Feng Xian, not sending them back.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan detected the plot and held Du Zheng and Feng Xian.

sentences.zh: 用安愈怒，謂德全、安國必有謀，乃執桃園帥吳某等八九人下獄鞫問。

translations.literal: Yong'an was still angrier, believing Dequan and Anguo must have a plot; he arrested Taoyuan commander Wu Mou and eight or nine others and interrogated them under torture.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Taoyuan's Wu and others, suspecting Dequan and Anguo.

sentences.zh: 二帥遣溫特罕張哥以杜政、封仙欲襲取徐州白用安，不聽，驅吳帥、張哥輩九人並斬之。

translations.literal: The two commanders sent Wentehan Zhang Ge to tell Yong'an that Du Zheng and Feng Xian meant to seize Xuzhou — he would not listen — and drove Wu, Zhang Ge, and nine others to be beheaded together.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Zhang Ge to warn him; he ignored it and executed nine men including Zhang Ge.

sentences.zh: 張哥將死大呼曰：「國咬兒，汝無尺寸功，受國家大封爵，何負於汝，而從杜政等變亂，又殺無罪之人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ge, about to die, shouted loudly, "State Bite-er, you have not an inch of merit yet received the state's great enfeoffment — what have we failed you, that you follow Du Zheng's mutiny and also kill the guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Zhang Ge cursed "State Bite-er" for rewarding treachery and murdering innocents.

sentences.zh: 今雖死，當與汝辨於地下矣。

translations.literal: Though I die today, I shall dispute with you underground.
translations.idiomatic: I will face you in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 」會上遣臧國昌以密詔徵兵東方，故用安假朝命聲言入援，檄劉安國為前鋒，親率兵三千駐徐州城下招德全。

translations.literal: " At that time the emperor sent Zang Guochang with a secret edict to summon eastern troops; therefore Yong'an used the court's command in name, proclaiming relief, ordered Liu Anguo as vanguard, and personally led three thousand troops stationed below Xuzhou city to summon Dequan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's secret summons let Yong'an claim he was marching to aid the throne while besieging Dequan.

sentences.zh: 德全終疑見圖，不出，系封仙於獄，殺之，遣杜政出城。

translations.literal: Dequan finally suspected he would be plotted against, did not come out, imprisoned Feng Xian, killed him, and sent Du Zheng out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan refused to emerge, killed Feng Xian, and expelled Du Zheng.

sentences.zh: 安國既至宿州，用安複召安國還，安國不從，獨與眾僧奴赴援。

translations.literal: Anguo having reached Suzhou, Yong'an again summoned Anguo back; Anguo did not follow but alone with Zhongsengnu went to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo reached Suzhou but ignored recall and marched with Zhongsengnu to aid the emperor.

sentences.zh: 行及臨渙龍山寺，用安使人劫殺之，遂攻徐州，逾三月不能下，退歸漣水。

translations.literal: When they reached Longshan Temple at Linhuan, Yong'an sent men to waylay and kill them; he then attacked Xuzhou; more than three months unable to take it, he withdrew to Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: At Linhuan's Longshan Temple he ambushed and killed them, failed for three months to take Xuzhou, and retreated to Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 於是，因世英以用安終不赴援，乃還朝，至宿州西，遇大兵，不屈而死，事聞，贈汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yin Shiying, because Yong'an ultimately did not come to the rescue, returned to court; west of Suzhou he met the great army and died without yielding; when the matter was reported he was posthumously made Defender of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shiying, seeing Yong'an would not aid the emperor, returned west of Suzhou, met Mongols, and died unyielding — posthumously Defender of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而用安軍食不給，乞糧于宋，宋陽許之，即改從宋衣冠，而私與朝使相親。

translations.literal: Before long Yong'an's army lacked food; he begged grain from the Song; the Song pretended to agree; he then changed to Song dress while privately keeping close to Jin envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Starving, he begged Song grain, donned Song dress, yet courted Jin envoys.

sentences.zh: 尋益乏食，軍民多亡去，乃命蕭均以嚴刑禁亡者，血流滿道。

translations.literal: Soon food grew still scarcer; soldiers and civilians fled in great numbers; he ordered Xiao Jun to use harsh punishments to forbid flight — blood filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: As more fled, Xiao Jun's draconian orders left blood on the roads.

sentences.zh: 大元東平萬戶查剌將兵至漣水，遂降焉。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan's Dongping ten-thousand-household Chala led troops to Lianshui; he then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol commander Chala of Dongping took Lianshui and Yong'an surrendered.

sentences.zh: 查剌既渡河，趨蔡州，用安以詭計還漣水，複叛歸於宋，受浙東總管、忠州團練使，隸淮閫。

translations.literal: Chala having crossed the river and hurried to Caizhou, Yong'an by a trick returned to Lianshui, again rebelled and returned to the Song, received Zhedong commissioner and Zhongzhou regiment trainer, subordinate to the Huai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Chala marched on Cai; Yong'an tricked his way back to Lianshui, rejoined Song as Huai commander.

sentences.zh: 甲午正月，聞大兵圍沛，用安往救之，敗走徐州。

translations.literal: In the first month of jiawu, hearing the great army besieged Pei, Yong'an went to rescue, was defeated and fled to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In jiawu's first month he failed to relieve Pei and fled to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會移兵攻徐，用安投水死，求得其屍，皮刂面系馬尾，為怨家田福一軍臠食而盡。

translations.literal: When troops shifted to attack Xu, Yong'an threw himself into the water and died; when his corpse was found, the skin of the face was flayed and tied to a horse's tail; the army of his enemy Tian Fu devoured the flesh piecemeal until none remained.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged at Xu, he drowned; his corpse was flayed and Tian Fu's men ate his flesh to the last scrap.

sentences.zh: 用安形狀短小無須，喜與輕薄子遊，日擊鞠衢市間，顧眄自矜，無將帥大體。

translations.literal: Yong'an was short in stature and beardless, delighted to roam with frivolous men, daily playing cuju in the market streets, looking about self-satisfied, without a commander's larger bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Short, beardless, and vain, he played cuju in the streets — no bearing of a commander.

sentences.zh: 介字介甫，平州人，正大元年經義進士第一，時為用安參議。

translations.literal: Jie, style Jiefu, a man of Pingzhou, first in classics in the first year of Zhengda, at the time was Yong'an's participating councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie of Pingzhou, top classics graduate of Zhengda 1, served as his councillor.

sentences.zh: 初，天祐等出汴，微服間行，經北軍營幕，至通許崔橋，始有義軍招撫司官府，去京師二百里矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tianyou and others left Bian, in plain dress they travelled by secret paths, passed northern army camps, reached Tongxu Cuiqiao — only then was there a Righteous Army Pacification Office, two hundred li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Tianyou left Bian in disguise, he passed Mongol camps to Cuiqiao — two hundred li from the capital — before finding any Jin office.

sentences.zh: 至陳州，防禦使粘葛奴申始立州事。

translations.literal: Reaching Chenzhou, Defender Nianshenu had just established prefectural government.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenzhou Defender Nianshenu was just organizing the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 留二日，至項城，縣令硃珍立縣事，有士卒千二百人。

translations.literal: Staying two days, reaching Xiangcheng, Magistrate Zhu Zhen had established county government; there were twelve hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangcheng Magistrate Zhu Zhen had twelve hundred men after five months' rule.

sentences.zh: 至泰和縣，縣令王義立縣已五月矣。

translations.literal: Reaching Taihe County, Magistrate Wang Yi had held the county five months.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe's Wang Yi had governed five months.

sentences.zh: 八月，至宿州，眾僧奴得報，且知朝廷授以權宿州節度使、兼元帥左都監之命，具彩輿儀衛出城五里奉迎。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, reaching Suzhou, Zhongsengnu received reports and knew the court had appointed him acting Suzhou commissioner and concurrent left commander of the supreme commander; he prepared colored carriage and guard to welcome five li outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month at Suzhou, Zhongsengnu learned he was named commissioner and marched out five li with full honors.

sentences.zh: 時東方不知朝廷音問已八月矣，官民見使者至，且拜且哭。

translations.literal: At that time the east had not had court news for eight months; officials and people seeing envoys arrive both bowed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The east had heard nothing from court for eight months; officials and people wept at the envoys.

sentences.zh: 有張顯者任俠尚氣知義理，即謂天祐曰：「東方不知朝廷音問已數月，今見使者，百姓皆感動。

translations.literal: There was one Zhang Xian, chivalrous and valuing principle, who immediately said to Tianyou, "The east has not known court news for several months; now seeing envoys, the common people are all moved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian, a man of honor, urged Tianyou: "Months without word from court — the people are moved to tears by your arrival."

sentences.zh: 若不以聖旨撫慰之，恐失東民之必。

translations.literal: If the imperial edict is not used to comfort them, I fear losing the east people's allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Without an imperial edict to reassure them, the east may turn away.

sentences.zh: 我欲矯稱制旨宣諭，如何。

translations.literal: I wish to falsely proclaim an edict to announce and instruct — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: May I proclaim an edict in the emperor's name? he asked.

sentences.zh: 」天祐書生，守規矩，不敢從，但以宰相旨集州民慰撫之，州民複大哭。

translations.literal: " Tianyou was a scholar, kept rules, dared not agree, but only gathered the prefecture's people by the chief minister's order to comfort them; the people wept again.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou, a cautious scholar, refused; he comforted the people by ministerial order, and they wept again.

sentences.zh: 明日，往徐州。

translations.literal: The next day they went to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they proceeded to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時青，滕陽人。

translations.literal: Shi Qing, a man of Tengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qing of Tengyang

sentences.zh: 初與叔父全俱為紅祆賊，及楊安兒、劉二祖敗，承赦來降，隸軍中。

translations.literal: At first he and his uncle Quan were both Red Scarves; when Yang An'er and Liu Erzu were defeated, they accepted amnesty and submitted, and were attached to the army.
translations.idiomatic: He and his uncle Quan had been Red Turban rebels; after amnesty they entered Jin service.

sentences.zh: 興定初，青為濟州義軍萬戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingding, Qing was ten-thousand-household of Jizhou Righteous Army.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xingding he commanded Jizhou's Righteous Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，叔父全為行樞密院經歷官。

translations.literal: At that time his uncle Quan was an officer of the Travelling Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Quan then served the Travelling Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 興定二年冬，全馳驛過東平，青來見，因告全將叛入宋，全秘之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xingding, Quan passed Dongping by post horse; Qing came to see him and informed Quan he would rebel and enter Song; Quan kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 2's winter Quan learned at Dongping that Qing meant to defect to Song and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 頃之，青率其眾入于宋。

translations.literal: Before long Qing led his followers into Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qing took his band into Song lands.

sentences.zh: 宋人置之淮南，屯龜山，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: The Song placed them in Huainan, stationed at Guishan, with a force of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Song posted them at Guishan in Huainan with tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，泗州行元帥府紇石烈牙吾塔遣人招之，青以書來。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding, Sizhou acting supreme commander Heshenlie Yawuta sent men to recruit him; Qing sent a letter.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 4 Sizhou's Yawuta sent envoys; Qing replied by letter.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「青本滕陽良民，遭時亂離，扶老攜幼避地草莽。

translations.literal: The letter said, "Qing was originally a good commoner of Tengyang; encountering the age's disorder, he led the old and young to flee into the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, "I was a peaceful man of Tengyang driven to the wilds with my family."

sentences.zh: 官吏不明此心，目以叛逆，無所逃死，竄匿淮海。

translations.literal: Officials did not understand this heart and regarded me as rebellious; there was nowhere to escape death; I hid in the Huai-Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Officials called me rebel; I hid on the Huai-Hai."

sentences.zh: 離親舊、去鄉邑，豈人情之所樂哉。

translations.literal: Leaving kin and old home, abandoning the native district — how is this what human feeling delights in?
translations.idiomatic: Exile from home is no man's joy."

sentences.zh: 僕雖偷生寄食他國，首丘之念，未嘗一日忘之。

translations.literal: Though I steal life and lodge eating in another state, the thought of returning home has not been forgotten a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Though I eat Song rice, I dream of home every day."

sentences.zh: 如朝廷赦青之罪，乞假邳州以屯老幼。

translations.literal: If the court pardons Qing's crime, I beg to borrow Pizhou to settle the old and young.
translations.idiomatic: Pardon me and lend me Pizhou for my families."

sentences.zh: 當襲取盱眙，盡定淮南，以贖往昔之過。

translations.literal: I shall raid and take Xuyi, fully settle Huainan, to atone for past faults.
translations.idiomatic: I will take Xuyi and recover Huainan to atone."

sentences.zh: 」牙吾塔複書曰：「公等初亦無罪，誠能為國建功，全軍來歸，即吾人也。

translations.literal: " Yawuta replied by letter, "You at first were also without guilt; if you can truly achieve merit for the state and return with the whole army, you are our man.
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta answered, "Return with your whole army and you are one of us again."

sentences.zh: 邳州吾城，以吾人居之，亦何不可。

translations.literal: Pizhou is our city; for our people to dwell there — what is impossible?
translations.idiomatic: Pizhou is ours — why not give it to you?"

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：'君子見幾而作，不俟終日。

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'The noble man sees the omen and acts, not waiting for the day's end.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says the nobleman acts when he sees the sign."

sentences.zh: '公其亟圖之。

translations.literal: ' Sir, plan it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Act quickly."

sentences.zh: 生還父母之邦，富貴終身，傳芳後世，與其羈縻異域，目以兵虜，孰愈哉？

translations.literal: Return to your parents' homeland, wealth and honor for life, fragrance handed to later generations — compared with being tethered in a foreign land and regarded as military captives, which is better?
translations.idiomatic: Come home to honor rather than live as a Song captive."

sentences.zh: 」牙吾塔奏其事。

translations.literal: " Yawuta memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta reported to court.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔加青銀青榮祿大夫，封滕陽公，仍為本處兵馬總領元帥、兼宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict added Qing Silver-Green Glory Grandee, enfeoffed Duke of Tengyang, and still made him commander of local troops and concurrent pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court enfeoffed him Duke of Tengyang and named him pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 青潛表陳謝，複以邳州為請。

translations.literal: Qing secretly submitted a statement of thanks and again asked for Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qing secretly thanked them and again begged Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 樞密院奏：「恐青意止欲得邳州。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized, "I fear Qing's intent is only to obtain Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat warned he only wanted Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 可諭牙吾塔，若青誠實來歸，即當授之。

translations.literal: Yawuta may be instructed: if Qing sincerely comes to submit, then grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tell Yawuta to grant Pizhou if he is sincere.

sentences.zh: 如審其詐，可使人入宋境宣佈往來之言，及所援官爵，亦行間之術也。

translations.literal: If his deceit is verified, men may be sent into Song territory to proclaim the exchanges and the official ranks granted — this is also a stratagem of sowing discord.
translations.idiomatic: If he deceives us, spread word of his offers in Song — a stratagem of discord."

sentences.zh: 」青既不得邳州，複為宋守。

translations.literal: " Qing, not obtaining Pizhou, again guarded for the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Denied Pizhou, Qing remained Song's man.

sentences.zh: 興定五年正月二十五日夜，青襲破泗州西城，提控王祿遇害。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the first month of the fifth year of Xingding, Qing raided and broke Sizhou's western city; Commander Wang Lu was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: On Xingding 5's first month, day 25, Qing stormed Sizhou's west gate and killed Commander Wang Lu.

sentences.zh: 是時，時全為同簽樞密院事，朝廷不知青襲破西城，止稱宋人而已。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Quan was concurrent Signing Secretariat Affairs; the court did not know Qing had raided and broken the western city, only saying it was Song men.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Quan was at court; they thought only Song troops had struck.

sentences.zh: 詔全往督泗州兵取西城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Quan to go supervise Sizhou troops to recover the western city.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was ordered to retake the west gate.

sentences.zh: 全至泗州，獲紅祆賊一人，詰問之，乃知青為宋京東鈐轄，襲破西城。

translations.literal: Quan reached Sizhou, captured one Red Scarve, interrogated him, and then knew Qing was Song Eastern Huai commander and had raided and broken the western city.
translations.idiomatic: At Sizhou he caught a Red Turban deserter and learned Qing had led the raid.

sentences.zh: 全頗喜，乃殺其人以滅口。

translations.literal: Quan was rather pleased and then killed the man to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased at the intelligence, Quan killed the prisoner to silence him.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔晝夜力戰，募死士以梯沖逼城，青縋兵出拒不得前。

translations.literal: Yawuta fought day and night, recruited dare-to-die men to press the city with scaling ladders; Qing lowered troops by rope to resist and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta assaulted day and night; Qing's rope troops held him off.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔遣提控王應孫穴城，東北隅，青夜出兵來襲，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Yawuta sent Commander Wang Yingsun to tunnel into the city at the northeast corner; Qing sent troops by night to strike and beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingsun tunneled; Qing's night attack repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 越二日，複出又卻之。

translations.literal: After two days they came out again and were again beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later another sortie failed.

sentences.zh: 攻城益急，青以舟兵二千合城中兵來犯牙吾塔營，提控斡魯朵先知，設伏掩擊，青兵大敗，溺淮水死者千人，自是不復出矣。

translations.literal: The siege grew urgent; Qing with two thousand boat troops combined with city troops to attack Yawuta's camp; Commander Woluduo knew beforehand, set an ambush, and Qing's troops were greatly defeated; a thousand drowned in the Huai; from this he did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's river assault was ambushed; a thousand drowned; he never sallied again.

sentences.zh: 王應孫穴城將及城中，青隧地然薪，逼出之。

translations.literal: Wang Yingsun's tunneling nearly reached inside the city; Qing tunneled, burned fuel, and forced them out.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsun nearly broke through; Qing counter-mined with fire and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 青乘城指麾，流矢中其目，餘眾往往被創，樓堞相繼摧壞，城中恟懼，遂無固志。

translations.literal: Qing stood on the wall directing; a stray arrow struck his eye; the rest were often wounded; towers and battlements were successively destroyed; fear arose in the city and there was no firm will.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow blinded one eye; walls crumbled; panic spread.

sentences.zh: 二月二十六日夜，青拔眾走，遂複西城。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-sixth day of the second month Qing withdrew his force and fled; the western city was then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth of the second month Qing fled; Sizhou recovered the west city.

sentences.zh: 五月，兵還，距淮二十里，諸軍將渡，全矯稱密詔「諸軍且留收淮南麥」，遂下令人獲麥三石以給軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the army returned; twenty li from the Huai the various armies were about to cross; Quan falsely claimed a secret edict "All armies for now remain to harvest Huainan wheat," and then ordered each man to obtain three piculs of wheat to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in the fifth month, Quan forged an edict to detain the army for Huainan wheat.

sentences.zh: 眾惑之，訛可及諸將佐勸之不聽，軍留三日。

translations.literal: The masses were perplexed; Eke and the various generals urged him but he would not listen; the army remained three days.
translations.idiomatic: Officers protested; he held them three days.

sentences.zh: 訛可謂全曰：「今淮水淺狹，可以速濟。

translations.literal: Eke said to Quan, "Today the Huai is shallow and narrow and can be crossed quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Eke warned the Huai was shallow and they must cross quickly.

sentences.zh: 時方暑雨，若值暴漲，宋乘其後，將不得完歸矣。

translations.literal: It is just the season of summer rains; if a sudden flood comes and Song follows behind, they will not be able to return intact.
translations.idiomatic: Summer rains might swell the river and trap them against Song pursuers.

sentences.zh: 」全力拒之。

translations.literal: " Quan forcefully refused.
translations.idiomatic: Quan refused.

sentences.zh: 從宜達阿、移失不、斜烈、李辛稍稍不平，全怒曰：「訛可一帥耳，汝曹黨之。

translations.literal: Congyi Da'a, Yishibu, Xielie, and Li Xin were somewhat displeased; Quan angrily said, "Eke is only one commander — you crowd are his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates murmured; Quan raged that they owed their posts to him.

sentences.zh: 汝曹致身至此，皆吾之力。

translations.literal: You have brought your persons to this point — all by my power.
translations.idiomatic: You are here because of me."

sentences.zh: 吾院官也，於汝無不可者。

translations.literal: I am a Secretariat officer; toward you there is nothing I may not do.
translations.idiomatic: As Secretariat officer I can do as I please with you."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃不敢言。

translations.literal: " The crowd then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: They fell silent.

sentences.zh: 是夜，大雨。

translations.literal: That night, great rain.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rains came.

sentences.zh: 明日，淮水暴漲，乃為橋渡軍。

translations.literal: The next day the Huai rose in flood; they then made a bridge to cross the army.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the Huai flooded; they bridged it.

sentences.zh: 宋兵襲之，軍遂敗績。

translations.literal: Song troops struck them; the army was then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Song attacked; the army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 橋壞，全以輕舟先濟，士卒皆覆沒。

translations.literal: The bridge broke; Quan crossed first in a light boat; soldiers all perished.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge collapsed; Quan fled in a light boat while his men drowned.

sentences.zh: 宣宗乃下詔誅之，遣官招集潰軍，詔曰：「大軍渡淮，每立功效。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor then issued an edict to execute him and sent officials to gather the scattered troops; the edict said, "The great army crossed the Huai and each time established merit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Quan executed and issued edicts recalling the scattered troops.

sentences.zh: 諸將謬誤，部曲散亡，流離憂苦，朕甚閔焉。

translations.literal: The generals erred; units scattered and fled; drifting in misery — We are deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: He lamented the generals' errors and the soldiers' suffering.

sentences.zh: 各歸舊營，勉圖自效。

translations.literal: Each return to your old camp; strive to renew your merit.
translations.idiomatic: Return to your camps and fight anew."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「陣亡把軍品官子孫，十五以上者依品官子孫例隨局承應，十五以下、十歲以上者依品從隨局給俸，至成人本局差使。

translations.literal: " Another edict said, "Descendants of fallen platoon and company officers of the fifteenth year and above shall follow the precedent for officials' descendants and serve in the bureau; below fifteen and above ten shall receive salary by rank in the bureau until adulthood and then be assigned by the home bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict cared for fallen officers' sons.

sentences.zh: 無子孫官，依例給俸。

translations.literal: Officers without descendants shall receive salary by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Childless officers' families were provided for.

sentences.zh: 應贈官、賻錢、軍人家口當養贍者。

translations.literal: Those due ennoblement, funeral money, and army households to be supported.
translations.idiomatic: Ennoblements, funeral funds, and dependents followed old rules.

sentences.zh: 並如舊制。」

translations.literal: All according to the old system."
translations.idiomatic: All as before."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金自章宗季年，宋韓侂胄構難，招誘鄰境亡命以撓中原，事竟無成。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: From the late years of Emperor Zhangzong, the Song's Han Tuozhou provoked trouble, enticing neighboring border fugitives to disturb the central plains; the affair in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy: after Emperor Zhangzong, Song's Han Tuozhou stirred trouble by harboring border fugitives — to no avail.

sentences.zh: 而青、徐、淮海之郊民心一搖，歲遇饑饉，盜賊蜂起，相為長雄，又自屠滅，害及無辜，十餘年糜沸未息。

translations.literal: Yet on the borders of Qing, Xu, and the Huai-Hai the people's hearts were shaken; year after year encountering famine, bandits rose like bees, each becoming a chief, again destroying one another, harm reaching the guiltless — for more than ten years boiling without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qing, Xu, and Huai-Hai boiled with famine, bandit chiefs, and mutual slaughter for a decade.

sentences.zh: 宣宗不思靖難，複為伐宋之舉，迄金之亡，其禍尤甚。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor did not think to settle the disorder and again undertook an expedition against Song; down to Jin's fall the disaster was still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong did not pacify the realm but attacked Song again — worsening Jin's fall.

sentences.zh: 簡書所載國用安、時青等遺事，至今仁人君子讀之猶蹙頞終日。

translations.literal: The brief records of Guo Yong'an, Shi Qing, and others' remaining affairs — until today humane gentlemen reading them still knit their brows a full day.
translations.idiomatic: Records of Yong'an and Qing still make humane readers wince.

sentences.zh: 當時烝黎，如魚在釜，其何以自存乎。

translations.literal: The common people of that time were like fish in a cauldron — how could they preserve themselves?
translations.idiomatic: The people were fish in a boiling pot.

sentences.zh: 兵，兇器也。

translations.literal: Arms are an inauspicious instrument.
translations.idiomatic: War is an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 金以兵得國，亦以兵失國，可不慎哉，可不慎哉！

translations.literal: Jin obtained the state by arms and also lost the state by arms — can one not be cautious, can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Jin won its empire by the sword and lost it by the sword — take heed, take heed!
